title: A concept is renamed by a version of its own kind; every reference follows the concept
situation: A concept whose recorded name redefines an established term is corrected by renaming it, and supersession is the only change to a concept, its name included: a renamed concept stays one concept, its earlier names in its history (record-speaks-the-pattern). The journal files every version under its concept's name, so a new name could only be recorded as a retirement and a fresh define, losing the concept's history and leaving every built-from reference to the old name dangling.
decision: (1) supersede takes an optional rename, the name the concept takes from this version on. A version given one is an entry of its own kind, rename: everything a supersede carries, its name the new one, plus was, the name it renames. A runtime that predates it reads it past and says its answer may be incomplete (0297), never showing both names live. (2) A concept is one through its versions whatever names they carry, its name its current version's: state and design show it under that name only; history, named by the current name or any earlier one, lists every version, each with the name it was recorded under and its reason. Every verb naming a concept takes its current name or an earlier one. (3) A built-from reference names a concept by the name it had when written; design shows each reference by the concept's current name, history exactly as recorded. (4) Within a context a name, once a concept's, stays that concept's for the journal's period: define refuses a name a concept of the context has had, naming the concept; a rename refuses a name another concept has or has had, and the concept's own current name; renaming back to one of its own earlier names is allowed. (5) While current versions compete and name the concept differently, it is listed among the competing under the name it had before them, each competing version showing the name it gives; a later version settles them as for any concept. (6) Closing the books opens a renamed concept as a define under its current name, and writes every opening's built-from with each reference's current name; its earlier names stay in the closed period.
consequences: A redefined term is corrected without losing its concept's history or breaking the concepts built from it. The journal holds a sixth concept-version kind; an older runtime reading a journal with a rename reports what it read past. One builder; review Ask.
